messages:
From: Lena Cruz <lena@cloudhealth.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, CloudHealth Ops <ops@cloudhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 03:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency + 5xx spike in us-west-2 AZ2 — impact on inference calls

Hannah / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp degradation in performance around 02:45 PT this morning that appears isolated to us-west-2 AZ2. Symptoms: p95 latency for text-generation calls has jumped from ~120ms to ~520ms, 5xx rate on model endpoints up to ~18% (was <1%), and overall throughput dropped ~38% as retries pile up. Customer dashboards and traces attached (we've included a pcap and a short trace export).

This is customer-facing — multiple production services are timing out. Can you confirm if this is a regional network/host-level issue or something on the routing tier? We need an explicit mitigation plan and an ETA. If you can initiate routing away from AZ2 to other AZs / regions we will coordinate the traffic cutover on our side.

Immediate asks:
- Confirm receipt and open an internal incident with exec awareness.
- Tell us expected time to stable routing fallback to other AZs and whether cross-region overflow is on the table.
- Recommended customer notice text (we will copy/paste once approved).

Thanks — this is high priority for our SRE and on-call.

Lena Cruz
VP, Platform Reliability
CloudHealth

Attachments: customer_traces_usw2_0728.pcap

Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 5xx spike in us-west-2 AZ2 — impact on inference calls

Lena —

We see it and have an incident active: INC-2028-0728-usw2. Thank you for the traces. Short answer: we are starting an immediate routing stabilization action and will keep you updated in 15–20 minutes.

Planned immediate mitigation (first 20 minutes):
- Policy-driven routing: begin draining AZ2 and redistribute new traffic across other AZs in us-west-2 (AZ1/AZ3).
- If tail latency persists after AZ drainage, enable cross-region overflow to us-east-1 (best-effort, with possible increased latency for some requests).
- Temporarily lower maximum batch size on the affected model family to reduce P95 tail.

We will post a short customer-facing note for you to send (draft below). Can you confirm you want us to activate cross-region overflow if AZ drainage does not stabilize within 25 minutes?

Draft customer notice (proposed):
"We are investigating elevated latency and error rates affecting a subset of servers in us-west-2 AZ2. Traffic is being routed away from the impacted AZ while we remediate; you may see reduced throughput or slightly higher latency as traffic redistributes. We will provide updates within 30 minutes and a post-incident summary afterwards."

Rishi / Marissa — please take action on the routing steps and share ETA. I will escalate to ops leadership and request approval for cross-region overflow and any customer credit decisions.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 28 Jul 2028 03:36:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency + 5xx spike in us-west-2 AZ2 — impact on inference calls

Quick tech summary and next steps (from infra):
Observed: noisy IO and GPU host-level I/O saturation affecting the host group serving AZ2. Host health checks show intermittent device stalls leading to degraded KV cache performance and longer serialization on the serving runtime; this amplifies tail latencies and increases 5xx.

Immediate actions I'm enacting now:
1) Activate routing policy to drain AZ2 and redistribute new sessions to AZ1/AZ3. This is a config change and should take 8–12 minutes to propagate.
2) Lower serving batch size for the affected model family by 30% (reduces queueing tail cost). Effective immediately, will reduce throughput but lower p95.
3) Start rolling reprovision of failing host slices in AZ2 (reboot + reprovision). This is longer (30–60m).
4) Prep cross-region overflow to us-east-1 if p95 doesn't drop under 250ms after AZ drain (estimate +12 min to enable and test).

Command snippets (ops runbook):
- route-control set-policy --zone us-west-2-az2 --drain=true --targets us-west-2-az1,us-west-2-az3
- runtime-set --model-family gen-2x --max-batch-size 32

ETA: routing changes active in ~10–15m, visible at customer edge ~12–18m. If we need to enable cross-region overflow, add ~15m test window.

I'll attach a short pcap and a collection of host logs to the incident.

— Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Jonas —

Forwarding the thread. Rishi has started the routing drain for AZ2; initial telemetry shows p95 beginning to fall but still elevated. We expect visible customer-side stabilization within ~20 minutes. If that does not meet the threshold (p95 < 250ms and 5xx < 1%), I request approval to:

1) Activate cross-region overflow to us-east-1 as a temporary mitigation (will increase some request latencies for a small fraction of calls).
2) Commit a service credit of 10% for the impacted window if SLA thresholds are breached.

Suggested customer communication once we confirm mitigation: (short)
"We have routed traffic away from the impacted capacity in us-west-2. You should see performance normalize over the next 30 minutes. We will follow up with a post-incident summary and remediation plan."

Please reply-all with an explicit go/no-go for cross-region overflow and credit approval so we can proceed. Time is sensitive.

— Hannah
